findings.fix: Collapsed runtime row now runs the same remedyFor() logic as per-name rows and gets remedyText/action when worst(runtime) === 'fail'.

evidence.test: CR-001: a failing runtime check gets a remedy on the collapsed row

findings.fix: remedyFor() filters all failing items for a name (not items.find's first match) and joins their unique hints.

evidence.test: CR-002: a check with two distinct failures surfaces both hints

findings.fix: showLogError() recreates the .health-log-error element when the container was wiped (e.g. by a racing showLoading()) instead of returning early and dropping the message.

evidence.test: CR-003: showLogError recreates the error banner after the container was wiped

findings.fix: createHealthController().run() carries a `running` busy flag mirroring installRunning; a second concurrent run() call is a synchronous no-op.

evidence.test: CR-004: a second run() call while one is in flight is a no-op

findings.fix: Zero parsed records renders showRunError()'s explicit could-not-determine state with a retry action instead of falling through to renderHealth()'s 0/0 summary.

evidence.test: CR-005: zero stdout records render an explicit could-not-determine state, not 0 of 0

findings.fix: run() wraps the runStream call in try/catch; a rejection renders showRunError() with a working retry action and calls onFailure(), which renderer.js wires to reset healthChecked so the one-shot auto-run guard is not permanently consumed.

evidence.test: CR-006: a runStream rejection renders a retry action instead of hanging, and reports failure; CR-006: the rendered retry action runs another doctor check

findings.fix: runHealthCheck's pipeline (stdout-tag filter, join, parse -> group -> render) was extracted into createHealthController() so the real call chain — not just the two pure functions — is exercised by a test that stubs runStream with mixed-tag lines.

evidence.test: CR-007: runHealthCheck pipeline renders only stdout-derived records

findings.fix: The open_log catch -> showLogError wiring (renderer.js's former inline onOpenLog) moved into health-controller.js's handleOpenLog() and is now directly covered.

evidence.test: CR-008: an open_log rejection surfaces through showLogError, not silently
